From medister (“minced pork mixed with fat”) + kake (“cake; patty”), literally “medister patty”.
The first element medister was borrowed through Danish medister, an alteration of Middle Low German metworst (“sausage made from minced pork”), influenced by ister (“suet, visceral fat”). The first element of the Middle Low German compound is met (“pork; minced meat”), from Old Saxon meti (“food, meal”), from Proto-Germanic *matją (“food”), traditionally from Proto-Indo-European *meh₂d- (“to drip, ooze; grease, fat”).
